verses.1: The LORD is a God of retribution, the God who executes justice. The LORD has taken up his case and has come forward to judge.
verses.2: Rise up, O judge of the earth, and give back to the arrogant what they deserve.
verses.3: How long, O LORD, will the wicked boast? How long will the wicked exalt themselves?
verses.4: They speak with arrogance, they devise violence; all who do evil plot.
verses.5: They crush your people, O LORD, and oppress your heritage.
verses.6: They murder the widow and the foreigner, and put the fatherless to death.
verses.7: They say, "The LORD does not see, the God of Jacob pays no attention."
verses.8: Take thought, you simple ones among the people; when will you understand, you senseless ones?
verses.9: The one who planted the ear—does he not hear? The one who made the eye—does he not see?
verses.10: The one who disciplines nations—will he not teach? The one who guides humankind—does he not instruct?
verses.11: The LORD knows all the thoughts of humankind, for they are but a breath.
verses.12: Happy is the one whom you, O LORD, correct, and whom you teach through your law.
verses.13: To keep him safe from days of calamity until the wicked fall into the pit.
verses.14: For the LORD will not abandon his people; he will not forsake his heritage.
verses.15: For judgment will return to righteousness, and all the upright in heart will follow it.
verses.16: Who will rise up for me against the wicked? Who will stand with me against those who do evil?
verses.17: If the LORD had not helped me, my soul would soon have dwelled in silence.
verses.18: When I said, "My foot is slipping," your steadfast love, O LORD, upheld me.
verses.19: In the abundance of my anxieties within me, your comforts have refreshed my soul.
verses.20: Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with you, you who plan evil by statute?
verses.21: They conspire to take the life of the righteous, and they condemn the innocent to death.
verses.22: But the LORD has become my refuge, and my God the rock of my protection.
verses.23: He will bring their guilt upon them, and in their wickedness he will destroy them— the LORD our God.

notes:
Notes
- v. 20: The Hebrew uses "cisai" (כִּסֵּא) as a poetic form of "fellowship" or "league," rather than a literal throne. The context of conspiring against righteousness supports the figurative rendering.
- v. 22: "Mitzva" (מַחְסִי) is typically translated as "refuge" or "protection," but the poetic use of "rock" supports a natural English rendering of "the rock of my protection."
